claim: Pathophysiological defects in water homeostasis can lead to renal failure.
source: Pathophysiological defects in water homeostasis can lead to renal failure.
evidence: This is a general statement about kidney pathophysiology that draws from established medical knowledge.

claim: Common genetic disorders associated with abnormal cytoskeletal dynamics in the kidney collecting ducts contribute to chronic kidney failure.
source: Likewise, common genetic disorders associated with abnormal cytoskeletal dynamics in the kidney collecting ducts and perturbed calcium and cAMP signaling in the ciliary compartment contribute to chronic kidney failure.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about genetic kidney disorders.

claim: Perturbed calcium and cAMP signaling in the ciliary compartment contribute to chronic kidney failure.
source: Likewise, common genetic disorders associated with abnormal cytoskeletal dynamics in the kidney collecting ducts and perturbed calcium and cAMP signaling in the ciliary compartment contribute to chronic kidney failure.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about ciliary signaling in kidney disease.

claim: Collecting ducts in mice lacking AKAP220 exhibit enhanced development of primary cilia.
source: We show that collecting ducts in mice lacking the A-Kinase anchoring protein AKAP220 exhibit enhanced development of primary cilia.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: AKAP220-associated protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) mediates the enhanced ciliogenesis phenotype in AKAP220 knockout mice.
source: Mechanistic studies reveal that AKAP220-associated protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) mediates this phenotype by promoting changes in the stability of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) with concomitant defects in actin dynamics.
evidence: This mechanistic finding is supported by experimental data from AKAP220-ΔPP1 knock-in cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: AKAP220-associated PP1 promotes changes in the stability of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6).
source: Mechanistic studies reveal that AKAP220-associated protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) mediates this phenotype by promoting changes in the stability of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) with concomitant defects in actin dynamics.
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase experiments and immunoblot data shown in Figure 2.

claim: AKAP220-associated PP1 mediates concomitant defects in actin dynamics.
source: Mechanistic studies reveal that AKAP220-associated protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) mediates this phenotype by promoting changes in the stability of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) with concomitant defects in actin dynamics.
evidence: This is supported by FRAP experiments and actin distribution analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: PP1 functions as an adaptor protein in the context of AKAP220-mediated ciliogenesis.
source: This proceeds through a previously unrecognized adaptor function for PP1 as all ciliogenesis and cytoskeletal phenotypes are recapitulated in mIMCD3 knock-in cells expressing a phosphatase-targeting defective AKAP220-ΔPP1 mutant.
evidence: This is supported by data from AKAP220-ΔPP1 knock-in cells shown in Figure 3.

claim: All ciliogenesis and cytoskeletal phenotypes are recapitulated in mIMCD3 knock-in cells expressing a phosphatase-targeting defective AKAP220-ΔPP1 mutant.
source: This proceeds through a previously unrecognized adaptor function for PP1 as all ciliogenesis and cytoskeletal phenotypes are recapitulated in mIMCD3 knock-in cells expressing a phosphatase-targeting defective AKAP220-ΔPP1 mutant.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Pharmacological blocking of local HDAC6 activity alters cilia development.
source: Pharmacological blocking of local HDAC6 activity alters cilia development and reduces cystogenesis in kidney-on-chip and organoid models.
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment experiments shown in Figures 3 and 7.

claim: Pharmacological blocking of local HDAC6 activity reduces cystogenesis in kidney-on-chip and organoid models.
source: Pharmacological blocking of local HDAC6 activity alters cilia development and reduces cystogenesis in kidney-on-chip and organoid models.
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment experiments in PKD2-/- organoids shown in Figure 7.

claim: The AKAP220-PP1-HDAC6 pathway is a key effector in primary cilia development.
source: These findings identify the AKAP220-PPI-HDAC6 pathway as a key effector in primary cilia development.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the collective experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Kidneys recycle about 180 liters of fluid every day to partition nutrients and remove toxins from blood.
source: Kidneys recycle about 180 liters of fluid every day to partition nutrients and remove toxins from blood (Saborio et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Saborio et al., 2000.

claim: Water reabsorption from luminal fluid is triggered by the hormone arginine vasopressin via phosphorylation-dependent translocation of aquaporin-2 water pores to the apical surface of kidney collecting ducts.
source: Water reabsorption from luminal fluid is triggered by the hormone arginine vasopressin via phosphorylation-dependent translocation of aquaporin-2 water pores to the apical surface of kidney collecting ducts (Bankir et al., 2013; Noda et al., 2010; Yui et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bankir et al., 2013; Noda et al., 2010; Yui et al., 2012.

claim: Approximately 35 million Americans suffer from chronic kidney diseases.
source: Approximately 35 million Americans suffer from chronic kidney diseases, characterized as a gradual loss of renal function (Hemmelgarn et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hemmelgarn et al., 2006.

claim: Chronic kidney diseases are characterized as a gradual loss of renal function.
source: Approximately 35 million Americans suffer from chronic kidney diseases, characterized as a gradual loss of renal function (Hemmelgarn et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a definitional statement supported by citation to Hemmelgarn et al., 2006.

claim: Polycystic kidney diseases are disorders where the collecting ducts become enlarged with fluid filled cysts that reduce glomerular filtration rate.
source: Polycystic kidney diseases are disorders where the collecting ducts become enlarged with fluid filled cysts that reduce glomerular filtration rate (Wilson, 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wilson, 2004.

claim: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) has an estimated prevalence of 1 in 600 people.
source: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with an estimated prevalence of 1 in 600 people, is a common genetic disorder associated with end-stage renal failure (Halvorson et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Halvorson et al., 2010.

claim: ADPKD is a common genetic disorder associated with end-stage renal failure.
source: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) with an estimated prevalence of 1 in 600 people, is a common genetic disorder associated with end-stage renal failure (Halvorson et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Halvorson et al., 2010.

claim: Clinical evidence indicates that primary cilia function is altered in ADPKD.
source: Clinical evidence indicates that primary cilia function is altered in ADPKD (Ma et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2017.

claim: ADPKD is classified as a ciliopathy.
source: Hence this chronic renal disorder is classified as a ciliopathy (Badano et al., 2006; Fliegauf et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Badano et al., 2006; Fliegauf et al., 2007.

claim: The primary cilium is a microtubule-based organelle protruding from the surface of most mammalian cells.
source: The primary cilium is a microtubule-based organelle protruding from the surface of most mammalian cells (Satir et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Satir et al., 2010.

claim: In the kidney, primary cilia respond to fluctuations in fluid-flow through collecting ducts.
source: In the kidney, primary cilia respond to fluctuations in fluid-flow through collecting ducts.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about ciliary function in the kidney.

claim: Primary cilia convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals to elicit developmental and regulatory responses.
source: They convert mechanical stimuli into biochemical signals to elicit developmental and regulatory responses (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2013; Somatilaka et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mukhopadhyay et al., 2013; Somatilaka et al., 2020.

claim: Disease causing mutations in the ciliary transmembrane proteins polycystin 1 (PKD1) and polycystin 2 (PKD2) underlie ADPKD.
source: Disease causing mutations in the ciliary transmembrane proteins polycystin 1 (PKD1) and polycystin 2 (PKD2) underlie ADPKD (Hughes et al., 1995; Mochizuki et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hughes et al., 1995; Mochizuki et al., 1996.

claim: PKD1 and PKD2 are components of a receptor-channel complex that responds to local second messenger signals.
source: Both proteins are components of a receptor-channel complex that responds to local second messenger signals (Harris and Torres, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Harris and Torres, 2014.

claim: A ciliary hypothesis has been formulated that implicates defective calcium and cAMP signaling in the ciliary compartment as a factor in disease progression.
source: Accordingly, a ciliary hypothesis has been formulated that implicates defective calcium and cAMP signaling in the ciliary compartment as a factor in disease progression (Ma et al., 2017; Winyard and Jenkins, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ma et al., 2017; Winyard and Jenkins, 2011.

claim: A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) spatially constrain second messenger regulated kinases, protein phosphatases, and GTPase effector proteins within subcellular compartments.
source: A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) spatially constrain second messenger regulated kinases, protein phosphatases, and GTPase effector proteins within subcellular compartments (Bucko and Scott, 2021; Langeberg and Scott, 2015; Omar and Scott, 2020; Smith et al., 2017; Smith et al., 2018; Taskén and Aandahl, 2004; Whiting et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations describing AKAP function.

claim: Several AKAPs participate in renal signaling.
source: Several AKAPs participate in renal signaling, yet only a few anchoring proteins reside in cilia (Choi et al., 2011; Gopalan et al., 2021; Jo et al., 2001; May et al., 2020; Stefan et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of AKAPs in renal signaling.

claim: Only a few anchoring proteins reside in cilia.
source: Several AKAPs participate in renal signaling, yet only a few anchoring proteins reside in cilia (Choi et al., 2011; Gopalan et al., 2021; Jo et al., 2001; May et al., 2020; Stefan et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of ciliary AKAPs.

claim: Ciliary AKAPs are postulated to position protein kinase A (PKA) as a negative regulator of hedgehog signaling.
source: Ciliary AKAPs are postulated to position protein kinase A (PKA) as a negative regulator of hedgehog signaling (Breslow et al., 2018; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2013; Somatilaka et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies of PKA in hedgehog signaling.

claim: AKAP220 is a multifunctional anchoring protein that sequesters PKA, GSK3, the Rho GTPase effector IQGAP-1, and protein phosphatase 1 (PP1).
source: AKAP220 is a multifunctional anchoring protein that sequesters PKA, GSK3, the Rho GTPase effector IQGAP-1, and protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) (Logue et al., 2011; Schillace and Scott, 1999; Whiting et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to studies characterizing AKAP220 binding partners.

claim: Each AKAP220-binding partner is implicated in local signaling events that potentiate ADPKD.
source: Each AKAP220-binding partner is implicated in local signaling events that potentiate ADPKD.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known functions of AKAP220 binding partners in kidney disease.

claim: PKA and PP1 bi-directionally control signaling in the ciliary compartment.
source: PKA and PP1 bi-directionally control signaling in the ciliary compartment, whereas reduced Rho GTPase activity contributes to expansion of renal cysts (Parnell et al., 2012; Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Parnell et al., 2012; Ye et al., 2017.

claim: Reduced Rho GTPase activity contributes to expansion of renal cysts.
source: PKA and PP1 bi-directionally control signaling in the ciliary compartment, whereas reduced Rho GTPase activity contributes to expansion of renal cysts (Parnell et al., 2012; Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Parnell et al., 2012; Ye et al., 2017.

claim: AKAP220 associated PP1 drives the enhanced ciliogenesis phenotype by promoting changes in actin dynamics and histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) stability.
source: Mechanistic studies reveal that AKAP220 associated PP1 drives this phenotype by promoting changes in actin dynamics and histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) stability.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 2-4.

claim: Changes in local HDAC6 activity alters cilia development and reduces cystogenesis in cellular models of ADPKD.
source: Changes in local HDAC6 activity alters cilia development and reduces cystogenesis in cellular models of ADPKD.
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment experiments in Figure 7.

claim: The AKAP220-PP1-HDAC6 pathway is a potential target for the HDAC6 inhibitor drug tubacin.
source: These findings point toward the AKAP220-PPI-HDAC6 pathway as a signaling center for the control of ciliary development and a potential target for the HDAC6 inhibitor drug tubacin.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tubacin experiments shown in Figures 3 and 7.

claim: AKAP220 modulates cytoskeletal signaling events through its ability to recruit kinases, phosphatases and the small GTPase effector protein, IQGAP1.
source: AKAP220 modulates cytoskeletal signaling events through its ability to recruit kinases, phosphatases and the small GTPase effector protein, IQGAP1 (Figure 1A; Logue et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Logue et al., 2011 and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: AKAP220KO mice display mild defects in water homeostasis.
source: AKAP220KO mice display mild defects in water homeostasis and altered aquaporin 2 (AQP2) trafficking that are linked to disruption of an apical actin barrier in the kidney collecting ducts (Figure 1B; Whiting et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Whiting et al., 2016 and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: AKAP220KO mice display altered aquaporin 2 (AQP2) trafficking.
source: AKAP220KO mice display mild defects in water homeostasis and altered aquaporin 2 (AQP2) trafficking that are linked to disruption of an apical actin barrier in the kidney collecting ducts (Figure 1B; Whiting et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Whiting et al., 2016 and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Altered AQP2 trafficking in AKAP220KO mice is linked to disruption of an apical actin barrier in the kidney collecting ducts.
source: AKAP220KO mice display mild defects in water homeostasis and altered aquaporin 2 (AQP2) trafficking that are linked to disruption of an apical actin barrier in the kidney collecting ducts (Figure 1B; Whiting et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Whiting et al., 2016 and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Deletion of AKAP220 correlated with increased numbers of primary cilia decorating each collecting duct.
source: Further investigation in kidney sections from wild-type and AKAP220KO mice led to the unexpected discovery that deletion of this anchoring protein correlated with increased numbers of primary cilia decorating each collecting duct (Figure 1C–H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C-H.

claim: There is a 3.5-fold increase in the percentage of ciliated cells in AKAP220KO collecting ducts compared to wild-type.
source: Analysis of tissue sections collected from several animals are presented in Figure 1I, measuring a 3.5-fold increase in the percentage of ciliated cells in AKAP220KO, as compared to wild-type.
evidence: This quantification is based on analysis of tissue sections shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Cilia in AKAP220KO collecting ducts are 1.68-fold longer than their wild-type counterparts.
source: Additional measurements determined that cilia in AKAP220KO collecting ducts are 1.68-fold longer than their wild-type counterparts (1.7 µm vs 1.02 µm; Figure 1J).
evidence: This measurement is based on quantification shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Loss of AKAP220 in mIMCD3 cells results in an 8- to 10-fold increase in the percentage of ciliated cells compared to wild-type.
source: Immunofluorescent detection of primary cilia in each AKAP220KO clone measured an 8- to 10-fold increase in the percentage of ciliated cells in comparison to wild-type mIMCD3 cells (Figure 1L–O).
evidence: This quantification is based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1L-O.

claim: Serum starvation of AKAP220KO cell lines enhanced detection of multi-ciliated cells.
source: However, serum starvation of AKAP220KO cell lines enhanced detection of multi-ciliated cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–G).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-G.

claim: Rescue with AKAP220 dramatically reduced the number of ciliated cells in AKAP220KO cells.
source: Quantification from three independent experiments confirmed that rescue with AKAP220 dramatically reduced the number of ciliated cells as compared to rescue with GFP (Figure 1U).
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 1P-U.

claim: Loss of AKAP150 alone had no effect on cilia development.
source: Immunofluorescent detection of ARl13b (green) and acetyl-tubulin (red) as ciliary markers revealed that the loss of AKAP150 alone had no effect on cilia development (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A & B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A & B.

claim: A pronounced increase in the ciliated population was observed in AKAP220/150 double knockout cells.
source: Yet, a pronounced increase in the ciliated population was observed in AKAP220/150 double knockout cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C & D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C & D.

claim: AKAP150 signaling does not support renal ciliogenesis.
source: These additional studies indicate that AKAP150 signaling does not support renal ciliogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the lack of effect of AKAP150 deletion on ciliogenesis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of AKAP220 correlated with persistence of primary cilia in mIMCD3 KO spheroids.
source: Immunofluorescent detection of the ciliary marker acetyl-tubulin (green) confirmed that loss of AKAP220 correlated with persistence of primary cilia in mIMCD3 KO spheroids.
evidence: This is supported by spheroid data shown in Figure 1W & X.

claim: Local signaling mechanisms that proceed through AKAP220 impact ciliary development in cellular, three-dimensional spheroid and animal models of the renal microenvironment.
source: Thus, local signaling mechanisms that proceed through AKAP220 impact ciliary development in cellular, three-dimensional spheroid and animal models of the renal microenvironment.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the collective data from cells, spheroids, and mice shown in Figure 1.

claim: Primary cilia formation requires tubulin heterodimers that are stabilized by acetylation on lysine 40.
source: Primary cilia formation requires tubulin heterodimers that are stabilized by acetylation on lysine 40 (Portran et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Portran et al., 2017.

claim: Acetylated tubulin is more prominent in AKAP220KO cell lysates as compared to wild-type.
source: Second, immunoblot analysis showed that acetyl tubulin was more prominent in AKAP220KO cell lysates as compared to wild-type (Figure 2C, top panel).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) catalyzes the de-acetylation of tubulin to promote depolymerization of primary cilia.
source: Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) catalyzes the de-acetylation of tubulin to promote depolymerization of primary cilia (Hubbert et al., 2002; Ran et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hubbert et al., 2002; Ran et al., 2015.

claim: The subcellular distribution of HDAC6 was altered in AKAP220KO mIMCD3 cells.
source: Conversely, the subcellular distribution of HDAC6 was altered in AKAP220KO mIMCD3 cells (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Deletion of AKAP220 correlated with a 50% reduction of total HDAC6 in mIMCD3 cells.
source: Amalgamated data from five independent experiments indicated that deletion of AKAP220 correlated with a 50% reduction of total HDAC6 in mIMCD3 cells (Figure 2J).
evidence: This quantification is based on immunoblot data shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Interface with AKAP220 serves to stabilize HDAC6.
source: This argues that interface with AKAP220 serves to stabilize HDAC6.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced HDAC6 levels in AKAP220KO cells shown in Figure 2.

claim: AKAP220/HDAC6 complexes were detected in cells transfected with V5-tagged AKAP220 using proximity ligation assay.
source: PLA puncta indicative of AKAP220/HDAC6 complexes were detected in cells transfected with V5-tagged AKAP220 (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 2K-O.

claim: In wild-type mIMCD3 cells, HDAC6 protein was relatively constant and acetylated tubulin levels were low during cycloheximide chase.
source: In wild-type mIMCD3 cells, HDAC6 protein was relatively constant and acetylated tubulin levels were low (Figure 2P, lanes 1–3).
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase data shown in Figure 2P.

claim: Upon loss of AKAP220, HDAC6 levels were markedly reduced over time and acetylated tubulin levels were elevated during cycloheximide chase.
source: Conversely, upon loss of the anchoring protein, HDAC6 levels were markedly reduced over time and acetylated tubulin levels were elevated (Figure 2P, lanes 4–6).
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase data shown in Figure 2P.

claim: Overexpression of murine HDAC6 abrogated primary cilia formation in AKAP220KO cells.
source: Finally, overexpression of murine HDAC6 (cyan) abrogated primary cilia formation in AKAP220KO cells (Figure 2R & S).
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2R-V.

claim: Expression of a catalytically inactive HDAC6 mutant had no effect on cilia formation in the AKAP220 null background.
source: In contrast, expression of a catalytically inactive HDAC6 mutant (H216A, H611A) had no effect on cilia formation in the AKAP220 null background (Figure 2T & U).
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2T-V.

claim: HDAC6 activity is implicated in AKAP220-mediated control of primary cilia development.
source: Collectively, these studies implicate HDAC6 activity in AKAP220-mediated control of primary cilia development.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the collective data in Figure 2.

claim: Dephosphorylation of HDAC6 favors its degradation.
source: Mechanistically, dephosphorylation of HDAC6 favors its degradation (Ran et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ran et al., 2020.

claim: Protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) is a well-characterized binding partner of AKAP220 that also interacts with HDAC6.
source: Protein phosphatase 1(PP1) is a well-characterized binding partner of AKAP220 that also interacts with this deacetylase (Brush et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on AKAP220-PP1 interaction and a citation to Brush et al., 2004 for PP1-HDAC6 interaction.

claim: PP1 may serve as an adaptor protein that bridges HDAC6 to AKAP220 at the ciliary compartment.
source: Therefore, we reasoned that PP1 may serve as an adaptor protein that bridges HDAC6 to AKAP220 at the ciliary compartment (Figure 2W).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the known interactions and illustrated in Figure 2W.

claim: Protein phosphatase one interacts with AKAP220 primarily through its KVQF motif.
source: Protein phosphatase one interacts with AKAP220 primarily through its KVQF motif (Schillace and Scott, 1999) and has recently been implicated in trafficking of polycystin-1 to cilia (Luo et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Schillace and Scott, 1999 and Luo et al., 2019.

claim: PP1 has been implicated in trafficking of polycystin-1 to cilia.
source: Protein phosphatase one interacts with AKAP220 primarily through its KVQF motif (Schillace and Scott, 1999) and has recently been implicated in trafficking of polycystin-1 to cilia (Luo et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Luo et al., 2019.

claim: AKAP220-ΔPP1 is unable to anchor PP1.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation assays confirmed that AKAP220-ΔPP1 is unable to anchor PP1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Removal of the principle PP1-interaction motif on AKAP220 negatively impacts association with HDAC6.
source: These data indicate removal of the principle PP1-interaction motif on AKAP220 negatively impacts association with HDAC6.
evidence: This conclusion is based on co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Loss of a mere four-residue motif that enables PP1-anchoring to AKAP220 correlated with dramatically increased cilia numbers.
source: Immunofluorescence experiments revealed that loss of a mere four-residue motif that enables PP1-anchoring to AKAP220 correlated with dramatically increased cilia numbers (Figure 3E & F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E-O.

claim: Primary cilia morphology is altered in the AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells, as compared to wild-type controls.
source: Additionally, the differential width of the three-dimensional surface plots show that primary cilia morphology is altered in the AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells, as compared to wild-type controls (Figure 3I & J).
evidence: This is supported by 3D surface plot analysis shown in Figure 3I & J.

claim: PP1 anchoring to AKAP220 is necessary for regulation of ciliary development.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that PP1 anchoring to AKAP220 is necessary for regulation of ciliary development and its loss is sufficient to drive enhanced ciliation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the AKAP220-ΔPP1 data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Loss of PP1 anchoring to AKAP220 is sufficient to drive enhanced ciliation.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that PP1 anchoring to AKAP220 is necessary for regulation of ciliary development and its loss is sufficient to drive enhanced ciliation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the AKAP220-ΔPP1 data shown in Figure 3.

claim: HDAC6 activity was reduced in AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1, as compared to the wild-type mIMCD3 cells.
source: As expected, HDAC6 activity was reduced in AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1, as compared to the wild-type mIMCD3 cells.
evidence: This is supported by HDAC6 activity assay data shown in Figure 3P.

claim: The loss of HDAC6 activity and elevated acetylated tubulin correlate with persistence of primary cilia.
source: These findings suggest that the loss of HDAC6 activity and elevated acetylated tubulin correlate with persistence of primary cilia.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: AKAP220-targeted HDAC6 modulates primary cilia development.
source: This led to a working hypothesis that AKAP220-targeted HDAC6 modulates primary cilia development.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the collective data presented.

claim: Application of tubacin (2 µM) increased the number of ciliated cells in wild-type mIMCD3 cells.
source: In wild-type cells, application of tubacin (2 µM) increased the number of ciliated cells as assessed by immunofluorescent detection of Arl13b (red) and acetylated tubulin (green; Figure 3R & S).
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment data shown in Figure 3R-X.

claim: Tubacin treatment resulted in a 3.2-fold increase in percent ciliated cells in wild-type mIMCD3 cells.
source: The gray scale image and quantification of three independent experiments reveal a 3.2-fold increase in percent ciliated cells upon pharmacologically targeting HDAC6 (Figure 3T & X).
evidence: This quantification is based on tubacin treatment data shown in Figure 3T & X.

claim: No change in cilia number occurred when AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells were treated with tubacin.
source: Importantly, no change in cilia number occurred when AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells were treated with tubacin (Figure 3U–Y).
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment data shown in Figure 3U-Y.

claim: AKAP220KO cells were unresponsive to tubacin treatment.
source: Similarly, AKAP220KO cells were unresponsive to the drug (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–D).
evidence: This is supported by tubacin treatment data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A-D.

claim: An HDAC6-PP1-AKAP220 signaling axis is the intracellular target for the drug tubacin.
source: This raises the intriguing possibility that an HDAC6-PP1-AKAP220 signaling axis is the intracellular target for the drug tubacin (Figure 3Z).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the differential response to tubacin in different cell lines.

claim: Covalent modification of cytoskeletal elements is an important facet of cytoskeletal regulation.
source: Covalent modification of these elements is an important facet of cytoskeletal regulation (Portran et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Portran et al., 2017.

claim: HDAC6 deacetylates the actin-binding protein cortactin to relocate it from the nucleus to its sites of action.
source: For example, HDAC6 deacetylates the actin-binding protein cortactin to relocate it from the nucleus to its sites of action (Ran et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ran et al., 2015.

claim: Nuclear accumulation of acetylated cortactin was more prominent in the nuclei of AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1 mIMCD3 cells, as compared to wild-type.
source: Immunofluorescent detection of acetyl-cortactin (green) was more prominent in the nuclei of AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1 mIMCD3 cells, as compared to wild-type (Figure 4A,C & E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A-G.

claim: AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells exhibit dramatic changes in the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Immunofluorescent analyses show that AKAP220KO and AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells exhibit dramatic changes in the actin cytoskeleton (red) (Figure 4H,J & L).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4H-M.

claim: Total loss of AKAP220 or disruption of HDAC6-PP1 attachment correlates with enhanced accumulation of cortical actin.
source: Line plot analyses (40–50 cells) reveal that total loss of the anchoring protein or disruption of HDAC6-PP1 attachment correlates with enhanced accumulation of cortical actin (Figure 4I,K & M).
evidence: This is supported by line plot analysis shown in Figure 4I, K & M.

claim: Disruption of AKAP220-signaling impacts the distribution and dynamics of actin filaments.
source: Thus, disruption of AKAP220-signaling impacts the distribution and dynamics of actin filaments.
evidence: This conclusion is based on FRAP and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The t1/2 for actin photo-recovery is 1.6 s in wild-type cells.
source: The t1/2 for photo-recovery is 1.6 s; n=106 (Figure 4R, gray).
evidence: This measurement is based on FRAP data shown in Figure 4N-R.

claim: The t1/2 for actin photo-recovery is 0.9 s in AKAP220KO cells.
source: In contrast, the t1/2 was 0.9 s; n=144 for AKAP220KO cells (Figure 4R, green).
evidence: This measurement is based on FRAP data shown in Figure 4N-R.

claim: The t1/2 for actin photo-recovery is 1.75 s in AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells.
source: Parallel FRAP experiments in AKAP220-ΔPP1 cells calculated a t1/2 of 1.75 s; n=128, representing a 0.85 + 0.10 s increase in the rate of photo-recovery as compared to wild-type (Figure 4R, blue).
evidence: This measurement is based on FRAP data shown in Figure 4N-R.

claim: Actin is a key regulator of cilia formation and elongation.
